articles.title: Welcome!
articles.contents:
Have you ever wondered why you can easily remember where you parked your car one day, but spend minutes on finding it another day? Or why some people are much more affected by a poor night’s sleep than for others? Such questions keep bothering me and that’s why I investigate them.
I mostly do so through experiments and mathematical modeling. In this way, I can get to the bottom of the processes underlying cognitive capacities like memory, learning, and decision-making. You can find my CV here.

News
February 22nd & March 21st, 2026: Kletskoppen festival and Donders Open Day
Together with Feline van Aagten, Kevin Reniers, and Lena Kohler, I represented the Lifespan Cognitive Dynamics lab at two outreach events. First Kletskoppen festival, where children learned all about language, and then the Donders Open Day, teaching visitors all about the brain and giving them a behind-the-scenes experience. We tested how different noise sources affect (fluctuations in) cognitive performance. Results coming soon!

December 18th, 2025: Symposium on the positive side of cognitive variability

September 16th, 2025: Symposium upcoming!
At the upcoming NVP Winter Conference, Rogier, Senne Braem, Marijn van Dijk, Janne Reynders, and I will organize a symposium on the positive side of cognitive variability. Our symposium will challenge attendees to think about potential positive aspects of variability, such as that it can be indicative of problem-solving skills, creativity, or developmental leaps. We discuss innovative ways to measure and quantify cognitive variability. Don’t forget to sign up!

September 1st, 2025: Learn all about (f)MRI
Next week it is time for the Donders Toolkit fMRI again. A crash course on everything you need to know about (f)MRI analyses. On Tuesday, I’ll tell you about ways to assess brain development using latent change score models, latent growth curve models, and non-linear methods.

articles.title: Science Communication
articles.contents:
Contents
Science festivals
Teaching packages and educational videos
Popular writing (articles and blogs)
Participation in the Hoe?Zo! Show (2020/2021)


I find it important and rewarding to communicate my findings in an understandable manner. As such, I try to come up with fun ways to show the public what I’m working on. Think of infographics, blogs, theater shows, exhibitions, etc.

Science festivals
Together with Feline van Aagten, Kevin Reniers, Lena Kohler, and Rogier Kievit, I respresented the Lifespan Cognitive Dynamics lab at Kletskoppen festival and the Donders Open Day. Two days full of inquisitive children and parents that asked us all about cognition and the brain and participated in our experiment on the effects of different noise sources on (fluctuations in) cognitive performance.



Teaching packages and educational videos
Together with Sophie Hofman, Feline van Aagten, and Rogier Kievit from the Lifespan Cognitive Dynamics lab, I developed teaching packages for elementary-school children. These packages include lectures and videos on being a scientist and on the brain, specifically on senses and memory.
Being a scientist


The brain: Senses


The brain: Memory


Popular writing (articles and blogs)
When I come across cool papers or news items about (the development of) cognitive performance and/or cognitive fluctuations, I like to write about it. I recently wrote a blog on the importance of science communication and on cognitive fluctuations in the context of the American presidential elections.
I also wrote an article on giftedness in adults for the trade journal De Psycholoog with clinical psychologist Pleun van Vliet. An example of the good things that happen when scientist meets clinician!
Participation in the Hoe?Zo! Show (2020/2021)
As a PhD student, I was lucky to participate in the award winning Hoe?Zo! Show, a science theater show for 9- to 10-year-olds developed by Barbara Braams and Lennart de Groot, and presented by Boy Vissers. The goal of the show was to get children excited about science while at the same time teaching the PhD students how to communicate science in an understandable manner. Over 500 children could ask their burning questions which I, together with fellow PhDs from a variety of fields, answered on the spot in a creative and age-appropriate manner. Our season was featured in Trouw and many local news outlets.

Most of my work concerns (computational) modeling of cognitive processes, including learning and decision making. I’m currently employed at the Lifespan Cognitive Dynamics lab at the Donders Institute in Nijmegen. Below you can find ongoing projects (feel free to reach out for potential collaborations!), and links and short author summaries of my papers; sometimes accompanied by slides and/or visual summaries of the papers.


You can find my dissertation on the development of reinforcement learning strategies here.
Ongoing projects
Time series
Continuous environmental monitoring of Dutch classrooms. In collaboration with Stijn Reits and Rogier Kievit (Donders/Radboudumc).
Time-of-day fluctuations in cognitive performance. In collaboration with Aline Korver (RUG) and Nick Judd (Stockholm University).
Cognitive performance and temperature. In collaboration with Aline Korver (RUG), Oystein Sorensen (Oslo University), and Nick Judd (Stockholm University).
The role of ambient noise in cognitive variability: A dynamic structural equation modeling approach. In collaboration with Afon Khari (UvA) and Rogier Kievit (Donders/Radboudumc).
Reinforcement learning
Inter- and intra-individual differences in exploratory behavior. In collaboration with Rogier Kievit and the CODEC team (Donders/Radboudumc).
Understanding, improving, and computational modeling of adolescents’ climate-friendly choice. In collaboration with Wouter van den Bos, Cameron Brick, Hilde Huizenga, Lucas Molleman, and Peter Verkoeijen (UvA, EUR, Avans).
Working memory use in reinforcement learning in older adults. In collaboration with Leendert van Maanen and Irene van de Vijver (UU).
